name: Honduras
headline: Honduras: +3.8% growth in 2025, 4.6% inflation, debt 40% of GDP
sections: Honduras is a $39.6 billion economy (2025), the world's 107th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.8% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $7,871 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 15.0% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.6% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 9.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.9% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 8.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 40% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 54% in 2020. The general government balance is −0.7% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +2.4% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 92% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.7% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 38% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 73.0 years (2024). Population: 11.0 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
